title: Firebase App Distribution
objectives: Understand App Distribution via a real-life analogy
Upload APK / AAB / IPA builds to tester groups
Automate distribution from CI (GitHub Actions / Fastlane / Codemagic)
Show in-app 'update available' via the Tester SDK
Fit App Distribution into a full multi-track release strategy

sections.markdown:
**Think of App Distribution as the private preview cinema for your app.**

Before a movie hits theaters, the studio invites critics + focus groups to a private screening — no ticket lines, no store review. **Firebase App Distribution is that private cinema for your app.**

- **Tester groups** — VIP invite lists: `qa`, `internal`, `beta`, `partners_india`.
- **Release notes** — the printed synopsis handed at the door: 'fixed login crash, new home layout.'
- **CLI / Fastlane upload** — the studio's private courier delivering the reel.
- **Email invitation** — the ticket. Tester taps → App Distribution app installs the build.
- **Tester SDK** — an usher inside the theater who taps you on the shoulder: 'a newer cut just dropped, want to swap?'
- **No store review** — the studio can screen new cuts hourly if it wants. Play/App Store 'internal tracks' also skip review but are slower to set up.

**Why every mobile team runs this pipeline:** waiting 2 hours for Play Internal → 24 hours for Play Alpha review just to get a QA build into a tester's hands kills iteration speed. Firebase App Distribution: `firebase appdistribution:distribute` → 30 seconds later testers have it. Combined with CI, EVERY commit to `main` can auto-produce a fresh build the whole company can install.

**Firebase App Distribution** ships pre-release Android APK / AAB / iOS IPA builds to invited testers **without going through the store**. Upload via **console, CLI, Gradle plugin, Fastlane, GitHub Action, or Codemagic**. Testers receive an email with a link → install via the Firebase App Distribution app (Android) or a signed provisioning profile (iOS). **Tester SDK** shows 'new build available' inside your app. Free at any volume. Great for internal QA + external beta; complements Play Internal / TestFlight for wider rings.

sections.markdown: ## CLI upload — the pattern every CI runs

sections.code:
# One-time login
npm install -g firebase-tools
firebase login

# Upload an Android AAB to tester groups
firebase appdistribution:distribute app-release.aab \
  --app 1:1234567890:android:abcd1234efgh \
  --release-notes-file release-notes.md \
  --groups "qa,internal,beta" \
  --testers "pm@company.com,designer@company.com"

# Upload an iOS IPA
firebase appdistribution:distribute app-release.ipa \
  --app 1:1234567890:ios:zzzz \
  --release-notes "fix login crash on iOS 17" \
  --groups "qa,internal"

# List releases / tester groups / testers
firebase appdistribution:testers:list
firebase appdistribution:group:list

# CI (GitHub Actions) — service-account auth
#   GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=/path/to/service-account.json
#   The service account needs 'Firebase App Distribution Admin' role.

sections.markdown: ## Fastlane + GitHub Actions example

sections.code:
# .github/workflows/nightly-distribute.yml
name: Nightly build → Firebase
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
jobs:
  distribute-android:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
      - run: flutter build appbundle --release --obfuscate --split-debug-info=./symbols

      # Firebase upload
      - uses: wzieba/Firebase-Distribution-Github-Action@v1
        with:
          appId: ${{ secrets.FIREBASE_APP_ID_ANDROID }}
          serviceCredentialsFileContent: ${{ secrets.FIREBASE_CREDS }}
          groups: qa,internal
          releaseNotes: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
          file: build/app/outputs/bundle/release/app-release.aab

      # Symbol upload — critical for Crashlytics readability!
      - run: |
          firebase crashlytics:symbols:upload \
            --app ${{ secrets.FIREBASE_APP_ID_ANDROID }} \
            ./symbols

sections.markdown: ## In-app 'new build available' via Tester SDK
## Common mistakes
**Mistake 1: Manual uploads from a laptop.** Someone forgets; QA gets no build. Automate ALL uploads in CI.

**Mistake 2: Distributing debug builds by default.** Debug flavor + missing obfuscation + Firebase collection enabled = polluted analytics + easy reverse-engineering. Distribute a **staging** flavor: minified, obfuscated, staging Firebase project, feature flags set for QA.
**Mistake 3: No release notes.** Tester gets 'new build v2.3.5' — has no idea what to test. Auto-populate from git log or PR description.

**Mistake 4: Forgetting to upload iOS provisioning profile.** Ad-hoc distribution needs each tester's UDID in the profile — Firebase collects them via the invite flow; must re-sign + re-upload when adding testers. Or use Enterprise / TestFlight instead.
**Mistake 5: Shipping the Tester SDK in Play Store release.** Includes debug scaffolding + Firebase-tester auth flows in prod. Gate behind flavor / build config.
**Mistake 6: Committing service-account JSON to git.** Full delete-project privileges. Use GitHub Secrets / KMS.
**Mistake 7: One 'testers' group for everyone.** Break into `qa`, `internal`, `design`, `partners`. Only send the relevant build to the relevant group; reduces noise.
**Mistake 8: No cleanup of stale testers.** Ex-employees still receive builds. Sync tester list to HR / IdP periodically.
## Best practices
**1. CI-only uploads.** No manual laptop uploads.
**2. Staging flavor** — obfuscated, staging Firebase, feature-flags for QA visibility.
**3. Auto-populate release notes** from commit message or PR body.
**4. Symbol upload alongside** — Crashlytics needs dSYM / mapping / debug-info to symbolicate crashes from distributed builds.
**5. Segmented groups** — `qa`, `internal`, `beta`, `partners_india`.
**6. Tester SDK behind a flag** — 'new build available' in staging only.
**7. Cadence: nightly → weekly → release**.** Nightly to internal, weekly to beta, release to Play/TestFlight.
**8. Rotate testers periodically** — HR / IdP-linked source of truth.
## Practice programs
**Practice 1 (Easy) — Upload from CLI.** Distribute one AAB to a `qa` group via `firebase appdistribution:distribute`.
**Practice 2 (Medium) — Automate from GitHub Actions.** On push-to-main, build + distribute to `qa`; verify tester email arrives.
**Practice 3 (Medium) — Tester SDK.** Show 'v1.2.5 available' dialog inside the staging build.
**Practice 4 (Hard) — Multi-ring pipeline.** Nightly → App Distribution; weekly → Play Internal / TestFlight; monthly → production.
**Practice 5 (Hard) — Signed + symbol-uploaded builds** — verify Crashlytics reports from distributed builds are symbolicated.
**Practice 6 (Expert) — HR-synced testers.** Cloud Function reads Google Workspace / Okta group membership; syncs to Firebase tester groups nightly.
## Interview Q&A

**Q1: How does App Distribution differ from Play Internal Testing and TestFlight?**

**A:** **App Distribution:** no store review; instant delivery to invited emails; free unlimited testers; works for AAB/APK/IPA. **Play Internal Testing:** ~2-hour review for the AAB signing chain to validate; up to 100 testers; free; delivered via Play Store (better upgrade UX, auto-updates). **TestFlight Internal:** no review; up to 100 dev-team members with App Store Connect roles; iOS-only. **TestFlight External:** ~1-day review; up to 10,000 testers by email invite or public link. **When to use each:** internal QA fast → App Distribution; iOS internal → TestFlight Internal; broader beta → Play Closed + TestFlight External; testing store-upgrade path itself → Play Internal. **Most teams run BOTH App Distribution (nightlies) + Play Internal (weeklies) + Play Open (release-candidate).**

**Q2: How do you automate distribution from CI?**

**A:** **(1) Service-account key** with `Firebase App Distribution Admin` role, stored in GitHub Secrets / KMS. **(2) CI job** — build Flutter app → `flutter build appbundle --obfuscate --split-debug-info=./symbols`. **(3) Firebase upload** — `wzieba/Firebase-Distribution-Github-Action` or `fastlane firebase_app_distribution`. Groups + release notes injected from the commit / PR. **(4) Symbol upload** — `firebase crashlytics:symbols:upload` — CRITICAL, or crashes are unreadable. **(5) Failure alerts** — CI job fails → Slack notification to the release channel. **(6) Multi-flavor** — separate jobs for `dev`, `staging`, `prod` targets; distribute to different tester groups. **Cadence:** every push-to-main → nightly; every tag → weekly; every release-branch → play internal + testflight. **Interviewers listen for the SYMBOL upload step + the flavor separation.**

**Q3: iOS ad-hoc distribution has UDID challenges — how do you handle them?**

**A:** iOS **ad-hoc** builds are signed against a provisioning profile that lists **each tester device's UDID**. When you invite a new tester through Firebase App Distribution: **(1)** They receive an email. **(2)** On tap, Firebase's tester app collects their UDID via a Safari profile install. **(3)** You must **re-sign** the IPA with an updated provisioning profile containing that UDID, then upload the new IPA. **Automation options:** Fastlane's `match` manages provisioning profiles + certificates in a shared git repo; the `firebase_app_distribution` action can auto-invite new testers via Fastlane. **The hassle** is a reason many teams **prefer TestFlight** for external iOS testing — no UDIDs to manage; Apple handles it. **Use App Distribution for iOS mostly for internal / signed-with-enterprise-cert scenarios.** Enterprise cert (paid Apple Enterprise Program) sidesteps UDIDs — but that program's scope is 'employee-only' + Apple audits it strictly.

**Q4: How does the Tester SDK work and when should you use it?**

**A:** The **Tester SDK** is a Firebase SDK gated to distribution builds: it (1) authenticates the tester via a Firebase-hosted OAuth flow, (2) checks for newer builds in App Distribution, and (3) if found, presents a native 'update available' dialog that installs the new APK. **Enables:** in-app 'you have a new build!' UX — faster than waiting for testers to open email. **Constraints:** DEBUG / staging flavor ONLY — don't ship this SDK in the Play Store release, or you leak an update path outside the store's control (against store policy + adds size). **Setup:** initialize behind a `kDebugMode || isStaging` flag; require sign-in only when a check is manually triggered. **Cadence:** on cold-start of staging build; or a manual 'check for updates' button in a dev-menu. **Fits into:** the internal QA loop — build lands in CI → email arrives → tester ignores it → but next time they open the app, the SDK offers the update in-place.

**Q5: How do you fit App Distribution into a full release pipeline?**

**A:** Multi-ring: **(1) Every PR merge to `main`** → CI builds `staging` flavor + distributes to `qa` group via App Distribution. Fast feedback for QA. **(2) Every green nightly** → distributes to `internal` (whole company) via App Distribution — dogfooding. **(3) Weekly Friday** → build a `beta` flavor (production Firebase project, feature-flags for beta cohort) → Play Closed Test + TestFlight External → external beta cohort. **(4) Release candidate** → tag `v1.2.0-rc1` → build + push to Play Internal + TestFlight Internal for last-mile QA. **(5) After sign-off** → promote same AAB / IPA to Production (Play → Open or Prod; App Store → prod submission). **Cadence rules:** app-distribution builds live 30 days (garbage collected); Play / TestFlight builds are permanent. **Symbolization + Crashlytics upload happen at every step.** Interviewers score highly on hearing about signing-key parity — nightly and prod share the same upload key so Crashlytics grouping works.

**Q6: What are common cost + security pitfalls?**

**A:** **Cost:** App Distribution itself is FREE — no per-tester / per-build charge. The real cost hides in **build-minutes** (GitHub Actions / Codemagic) — parallel iOS + Android + staging + release matrix explodes fast. Batch smart; run staging only on `main`, not every branch. **Security:** **(1) Service-account key with App Distribution Admin role** = broad delete-any-release rights. Rotate + scope to only App Distribution. **(2) Signing keys** — Android upload/signing keys must live in KMS / Play App Signing; never in the repo. iOS certificates in Fastlane match (encrypted git). **(3) Stale testers** — auto-remove ex-employees. **(4) Public download links** — App Distribution's tester-invite URLs are non-guessable but shareable; treat as sensitive. **(5) Enterprise cert (iOS) misuse** — Apple revokes it if you distribute to non-employees; use TestFlight for that instead. **(6) Debug SDKs in prod** — always flavor-gate the Tester SDK.

## Real-world usage

- **Nightly QA loop** — every mobile team.
- **External beta** — invite a partner or key customer to test a new feature before public launch.
- **Feature-branch previews** — CI distributes a build per-feature-branch to designers for review.
- **Sales demos** — hand a customer an early build for a demo.
- **Bug repro** — 'here's a build with extra logging'.
- **Not the same as** Play/TestFlight — those are for wider beta + store-signing validation.

## Advanced notes

- **Automatic release-notes from git log** — `git log --pretty=format:'- %s (%h)' HEAD~10..HEAD`.
- **Multi-flavor CI** — matrix over `(platform, flavor)` — Android+iOS × dev+staging+release.
- **Fastlane `firebase_app_distribution` plugin** — full Fastlane integration incl. auto-invite testers.
- **Codemagic + Firebase App Distribution** — first-class checkbox in Codemagic workflows.
- **Deep links to specific tester group** — App Distribution URLs can carry group context.
- **Auto-cleanup** — App Distribution releases expire after 30 days; keep production release process for archival.
- **In-app 'What's new' dialog** — on tester install, show a full-screen release-notes screen (build with Remote Config).
- **Analytics on distributions** — App Distribution surfaces install rate per tester group.
- **Feedback tab** — testers can send text feedback + screenshots (paid feature or via 3rd-party plugin).
- **Programmatic API** — REST endpoint for CI-driven distribution when Fastlane / CLI isn't a fit.
- **Rate limits** — very generous; not a practical concern.
- **Signing parity** — Crashlytics groups by signature; parity between nightly + prod signing preserves grouping.
